Linear correspondence constraints for alignment coefficients

Source: R/linear_constraints.R
linear_correspondence.Rd

Describe soft agreement between linear summaries of two domains' projection coefficients. For maps H1 and H2, coefficients W1 and W2, and effective row weights d, the added objective is strength * sum(d * rowSums((H1 %*% W1 - H2 %*% W2)^2)).

Usage

linear_correspondence(
  domains,
  maps,
  weights = 1,
  strength = 1,
  reduction = c("weighted_mean", "sum"),
  name = "correspondence",
  space = "processed"
)

Arguments

domains

Character vector of two distinct domain names, matching the names in the alignment input.

maps

List of two finite numeric matrices (base or Matrix), with equal positive row counts. Columns index each domain's processed input features. Different domains may have different numbers of features. If row names are supplied, both maps must have identical, unique row names in order. Named columns must exactly match the processed data's feature names.

weights

Nonnegative finite confidence weights, one per matched row, or a scalar recycled across rows. Zero weights omit individual links.

strength

Finite nonnegative multiplier for this constraint.

reduction

"weighted_mean" divides weights by their sum; "sum" retains their absolute magnitude. Neither option rescales the maps or harmonizes their units. An all-zero weighted mean is undefined.

name

Nonempty label for diagnostics; labels must be unique within a fit.

space

Coordinate contract. Currently only "processed" is supported: maps act on coefficients after input preprocessing but before SSMA's internal compression. Maps are never centered or standardized as samples.

Value

A linear_alignment_constraint object. Pass a list of these objects to ssma_align() via constraints. Currently SSMA is the consumer.

Details

These are homogeneous quadratic soft constraints, not additional samples or hard equalities. They do not modify sample neighborhoods or their degree normalization. Selecting feature coefficients, averaging groups, and applying linear measurement maps all use the same interface. For processed data X, maps A %*% X express correspondence between weighted sample summaries A.

With externally reduced input Z = X %*% P, use maps H %*% P and compose returned coefficients as P %*% W. With covariance maps, calculate G %*% crossprod(X, Z) / (nrow(X) - 1) for centered data instead of forming the full feature covariance. Covariance estimation and preprocessing belong to the caller and must respect validation folds.

Unnamed columns are interpreted positionally. Raw-space constraints are not automatically transformed through arbitrary preprocessing. For a known linear preprocessing map S, a raw-coefficient functional H becomes H S; intercepts are outside this homogeneous coefficient contract.

Examples

h <- diag(3)
link <- linear_correspondence(c("a", "b"), list(h, h), name = "features")
smooth <- linear_penalty("a", diff(diag(3)), name = "smoothness")
